question: In the Basic Control Skills test, what is scored as a 'pull-up'?
choice_a: Setting the parking brake before exiting the vehicle
choice_b: Sounding the horn at the end of an exercise
choice_c: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
choice_d: Stopping the vehicle without changing direction
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position, and notes that stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Pull-Ups

question: Which two Basic Control Skills exercises specifically score pull-ups?
choice_a: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
choice_b: All four exercises equally
choice_c: Only Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
choice_d: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
explanation: The manual states pull-ups are scored on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Pull-Ups

question: What counts as an 'encroachment' during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors or unique parts at/above door mirror height
choice_b: Stopping the vehicle mid-exercise
choice_c: Only completely crossing the outer boundary line
choice_d: Any contact with a cone regardless of which vehicle part touches it
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the vehicle's mirrors or other unique parts at or higher than door mirror height.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Encroachments

question: What is scored as a 'look' during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Checking the mirrors from the driver's seat
choice_b: Sounding the horn upon completion of an exercise
choice_c: Asking the examiner a clarifying question
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle (or, on a bus, walking to the back) to check the vehicle's position while performing an exercise
explanation: The manual states a driver is scored for a 'look' when exiting the vehicle, or on a bus walking to the back to get a better view, while performing a backing exercise.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Looks

question: How many free looks are allowed on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) compared to Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: Two free looks on Exercise 2, and one free look on Exercise 4
choice_b: No free looks are allowed on either exercise
choice_c: Unlimited free looks on both exercises
choice_d: A maximum of one free look on Exercise 2, and two free looks on Exercise 4
explanation: The manual states a driver may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Looks

question: What must a driver do before exiting the vehicle to check its position during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and safely exit facing the vehicle while maintaining three points of contact
choice_b: Honk the horn twice before exiting
choice_c: Simply open the door and step out
choice_d: Turn off the engine completely before doing anything else
explanation: The manual requires that when exiting or entering the vehicle, the driver must set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Looks

question: What can result from failing to safely secure the vehicle or safely exit/enter it during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: An automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_b: A verbal warning with no penalty
choice_c: A single point deduction with no further penalty
choice_d: A requirement to repeat only that exercise
explanation: The manual states that if a driver does not safely secure the vehicle or safely exit/enter it, it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Looks

question: What happens if a driver opens the vehicle door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral/park) during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: It has no consequence if brief
choice_b: It only counts as a 'look'
choice_c: It results only in a warning to close the door
choice_d: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
explanation: The manual states that if a driver opens the door while the vehicle is moving, it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Looks

question: On which two exercises is a driver scored for 'final position'?
choice_a: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
choice_b: All four exercises
choice_c: Final position is not scored on any exercise
choice_d: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
explanation: The manual states the driver will be scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Final Position

question: What must a driver do upon completion of each Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Turn off the engine entirely
choice_b: Immediately proceed to the next exercise without stopping
choice_c: Exit the vehicle and report directly to the examiner
choice_d: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn
explanation: The manual states that upon completion of an exercise, the driver must set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn to indicate completion.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: In Exercise 1 (Forward Stop), where must the driver stop the vehicle?
choice_a: The driver may stop multiple times to adjust position
choice_b: As close to the cones as possible, with touching allowed
choice_c: With the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley, without going past it, stopping only once
choice_d: Anywhere within the alley boundaries
explanation: The manual states the driver must stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it, and may stop only once.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing), how far must the driver back the vehicle?
choice_a: Straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end
choice_b: Until instructed to stop by a horn signal
choice_c: Only halfway through the alley
choice_d: Until the rear of the vehicle touches the starting cones
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to back straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed during Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing)?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and two exits
choice_b: One free pull-up, and the driver may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around it
choice_c: Unlimited pull-ups and exits
choice_d: No pull-ups or exits are allowed on this exercise
explanation: The manual states the driver is allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around the vehicle during Exercise 2.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What must a driver maintain while completing Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)?
choice_a: A complete stop at the midpoint of the exercise
choice_b: The vehicle's left tires directly on the center line
choice_c: A constant speed of exactly 5 mph
choice_d: The right most rear tire between the cone and the line without stopping
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to keep the right most rear tire between the cone and the line without stopping while steering left through the opening into the opposite lane.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What happens if a driver stops, backs up, or exits the vehicle during Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)?
choice_a: Nothing happens, since stopping is permitted
choice_b: The exercise will be ended
choice_c: The driver must restart the exercise from the beginning
choice_d: Points are deducted but the exercise continues
explanation: The manual states the driver is not allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during Exercise 3, and if the driver stops, the exercise will be ended.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), how close must the rear most part of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Exactly touching the rear boundary line
choice_b: It does not need to reach the rear area at all
choice_c: Within three feet of the rear of the alley
choice_d: Within ten feet of the rear of the alley
explanation: The manual states the driver must bring the rear most part of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley and stop with it in the three-foot box.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed during Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: Unlimited pull-ups and exits
choice_b: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_c: Two free pull-ups, and the driver may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around it
choice_d: No pull-ups or exits are allowed on this exercise
explanation: The manual states the driver is allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around it during Exercise 4.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must a driver do if they back beyond the rear boundary of the alley during Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: Continue backing until told to stop by the examiner
choice_b: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise
choice_c: Immediately fail the exercise with no chance to recover
choice_d: Exit the vehicle and manually reposition it
explanation: The manual states that if a driver backs beyond the rear boundary of the alley, they must pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must be passed before a driver can attempt the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: The written knowledge test only, with no practical prerequisite
choice_b: A supervised road test with an instructor
choice_c: There is no prerequisite for the Basic Control Skills test
choice_d: The Vehicle Inspection test
explanation: The manual states the Vehicle Inspection test must be passed before a driver can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: What must be passed before a driver can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: There is no prerequisite for the Road Test
choice_b: A separate parking examination
choice_c: The Basic Control Skills test
choice_d: Only the Vehicle Inspection test
explanation: The manual states the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before a driver can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Road Test

question: What must a driver do when approaching a turn during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Accelerate to clear the intersection more quickly
choice_b: Turn off the turn signal immediately after starting the turn
choice_c: Coast in neutral through the entire turn
choice_d: Use turn signals to warn others, slow down smoothly, and change gears as needed without unsafe coasting
explanation: The manual instructs that as a driver approaches a turn, they must use turn signals to warn others of the turn, slow down smoothly, and change gears as needed while not coasting unsafely.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: How does the manual define 'unsafe coasting'?
choice_a: Coasting for more than ten seconds regardless of distance
choice_b: Any coasting while traveling downhill
choice_c: Coasting while using cruise control
choice_d: When the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: What must a driver do while driving through an intersection during the on-road test?
choice_a: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions, decelerate, and yield to pedestrians and traffic in the intersection
choice_b: Change lanes to find a faster path through the intersection
choice_c: Sound the horn to warn cross traffic
choice_d: Accelerate to beat oncoming cross traffic
explanation: The manual states that when driving through an intersection, the driver must check traffic thoroughly in all directions, decelerate, and yield to any pedestrians and traffic in the intersection.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: What is required before making a lane change during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: No signal is required if the road appears empty
choice_b: Change lanes only when directly instructed mid-maneuver without checking traffic
choice_c: Signal only after beginning the lane change
choice_d: Make necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so
explanation: The manual states the driver should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: What must a driver do before entering an expressway during the on-road test?
choice_a: Enter at the posted speed limit regardless of surrounding traffic flow
choice_b: Merge without signaling if traffic appears light
choice_c: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
choice_d: Stop completely before merging onto the expressway
explanation: The manual states that before entering the expressway, the driver must check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, what must a driver do before pulling back into traffic?
choice_a: Immediately release the parking brake and accelerate
choice_b: Skip checking traffic since the flashers are already activated
choice_c: Check traffic and mirrors thoroughly in all directions, turn off the four-way flashers, activate the left turn signal, then release the parking brake and pull straight ahead when safe
choice_d: Turn the steering wheel before the vehicle begins to move
explanation: The manual instructs that when resuming, the driver must check traffic and mirrors thoroughly, turn off the four-way flashers, activate the left turn signal, and only then release the parking brake and pull straight ahead when traffic permits.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: What should a driver do before entering a curve during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Shift to neutral while traveling through the curve
choice_b: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_c: Brake continuously throughout the entire curve
choice_d: Reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
explanation: The manual states that before entering a curve, the driver should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: For vehicles required to stop at railroad crossings (such as buses or vehicles displaying placards), how far from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop?
choice_a: At least 100 feet away from the nearest rail
choice_b: Within 5 feet of the nearest rail
choice_c: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Exactly at the rail itself
explanation: The manual states such vehicles must stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: What must a driver avoid doing while any part of the vehicle is crossing railroad tracks?
choice_a: Stopping, changing gears, or changing lanes
choice_b: Using the horn
choice_c: Maintaining a constant speed
choice_d: Checking the mirrors
explanation: The manual states a driver must not stop, change gears, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is proceeding across the tracks.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: For a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle approaching a non-exempt railroad crossing, when should the four-way flashers be deactivated?
choice_a: They are not required at railroad crossings
choice_b: They should remain on for the rest of the trip
choice_c: Before the vehicle stops to check for a train
choice_d: After the vehicle crosses the tracks
explanation: The manual states the four-way flashers should be deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: What might a driver be asked to identify after driving under an overpass or over a bridge during the on-road test?
choice_a: The exact number of support columns
choice_b: The name of the engineer who designed the structure
choice_c: The posted clearance/height or the posted weight limit
choice_d: The bridge's construction date
explanation: The manual states the driver may be asked to tell the examiner the posted clearance or height after an overpass, or the posted weight limit after a bridge.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: During a student discharge exercise for a School Bus endorsement, how far away from students must the school bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 10 feet away
choice_b: At least 50 feet away
choice_c: There is no minimum distance specified
choice_d: Exactly 3 feet away
explanation: The manual states the driver must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: For vehicles with an unsynchronized manual transmission, what shifting technique must a driver use during the on-road test?
choice_a: Float the gears without ever using the clutch
choice_b: No clutch use is needed for unsynchronized transmissions
choice_c: Double-clutch when shifting
choice_d: Single-clutch shifting only
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, the driver must double-clutch when shifting.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What gear-related behavior is prohibited during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Downshifting before coming to a stop
choice_b: Selecting the correct gear for the vehicle's speed
choice_c: Grinding or clashing gears, and shifting in turns and intersections
choice_d: Choosing a gear that avoids revving or lugging the engine
explanation: The manual states a driver should not grind or clash gears and should not shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What braking technique is required during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Apply maximum brake pressure at all times
choice_b: Ride the brake continuously on downhill grades
choice_c: Pump the brakes rapidly for maximum stopping power
choice_d: Brake smoothly using steady pressure, without riding or pumping the brake or braking harshly
explanation: The manual states the driver should not ride or pump the brake, should not brake harshly, and should brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: According to the lane usage standards, where should a driver finish a left turn on a multiple lane road?
choice_a: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: In the same lane the turn started from
choice_c: In the left-most lane regardless of the turn's direction
choice_d: In any open lane available at the time
explanation: The manual states a driver should complete a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line on a multiple lane road.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Where should a driver finish a right turn according to the lane usage standards?
choice_a: In the left-most lane to prepare for a future turn
choice_b: In the center lane of a multi-lane road
choice_c: In whichever lane has the least traffic
choice_d: In the right-most (curb) lane
explanation: The manual states a driver should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: What is required regarding hand position on the steering wheel during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Hands may be removed from the wheel while stopped at a light
choice_b: One hand may remain on the wheel at all times while the other operates accessories
choice_c: Only one hand is required on straightaways
choice_d: Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, then return both hands once the shift is complete
explanation: The manual states a driver should keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, and should return both hands to the wheel once the shift is complete.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

question: When must a driver check mirrors and traffic according to the regular traffic checks standard?
choice_a: Regularly, and specifically before, while in, and after an intersection
choice_b: Only when changing lanes
choice_c: Only when instructed to do so by the examiner
choice_d: Only at the start of the driving test
explanation: The manual states a driver must check mirrors and traffic regularly, and specifically before, while in, and after an intersection.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

question: What must a driver do with turn signals upon completing a turn or lane change?
choice_a: Turn signals cancel automatically and require no driver action
choice_b: Cancel the turn signal
choice_c: Switch on the opposite turn signal to indicate completion
choice_d: Leave the turn signal on for the next several intersections
explanation: The manual states a driver must cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals

question: What must a driver do if the test route does not include a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Request that the test be rescheduled to a different route
choice_b: Automatically fail that section of the test
choice_c: Skip that portion of the test entirely with no discussion
choice_d: Tell the examiner what the driver is doing or would be doing if they were in that traffic situation
explanation: The manual states that if the test route does not have certain traffic situations, the driver may be asked to simulate the situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: During the urban business portion of the on-road test, how should a driver position the vehicle in the lane?
choice_a: Straddling the lane markings for maximum visibility
choice_b: Centered in the proper (right-most) lane while keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_c: As far left in the lane as possible to avoid parked cars
choice_d: In whichever lane has the fewest pedestrians nearby
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and the driver should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business
